clue.text: Butler who wrote a book

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name of ... Butler, the Victorian novelist who wrote Erewhon and The Way of All Flesh
second meaning: a book of the Old Testament (two books, in fact)

explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant, but it is the surname of a writer; the answer is his first name and also a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler was the author of Erewhon, and First and Second Samuel are books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: E.g. George taken in by identical swindle

indicators.note: taken in by means the king goes inside the word for identical

parts.note: same means identical
George is the name of several British kings, so an example of a king

explanation.surface: Someone named George is duped by an identical twin's con.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin game is an American expression for a rigged gambling game or fraud.

clue.text: No 6D (as translated) in masterwork

indicators.note: as translated means these letters are rendered into a different form, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 6 down, a sausage

explanation.surface: A clue saying a sausage, in translation, isn't a masterpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait of Lisa Gherardini is perhaps the most famous painting in the world, a masterpiece.

clue.text: Film shown on Scot's little box

indicators.note: shown on means, in a down clue, that the film's letters sit above the Scottish word

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's 1982 film about an extraterrestrial
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A film shown on a Scotsman's tiny television set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a TV, as in the goggle-box, but means a small case.
explanation.definitionFit: An etwee (or etui) is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Old king has heir, a buffoon in charge for a spell

definitions.text: a buffoon in charge for a spell

parts.note: John was an English king of the 13th century
a son is an heir

explanation.surface: An old monarch's successor turns out to be a clown who briefly held power.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Boris Johnson, the UK prime minister from 2019 to 2022, often portrayed as a buffoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson, the clownish British prime minister, held office for only about three years.

clue.text: Daughter in jail beginning to expect justice

indicators.note: in means the daughter's letter goes inside the jail word

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of expect

parts.note: taken for its first letter

explanation.surface: A daughter in prison starts to expect a fair hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Justice' reads as fairness, but here it is a person, as in a Justice of the Peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a title for a judge, as in Mr Justice Smith or a Supreme Court justice.

clue.text: Terrible endless night, 24D having nightmares

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters are thrown into disorder
endless means the last letter of night is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its end is lost
the answer to 24 down, a snake

explanation.surface: A snake suffers a dreadful night of bad dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' turns NIGHT into NIGH; with ADDER from 24 down, 'Terrible' rearranges NIGHADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hag-ridden means tormented, originally by a witch thought to sit on sleepers, giving bad dreams.

clue.text: SAUSAGE! The writer's unfortunately upset

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read from the bottom up

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, and 'the writer's' is I'M, I am
alas is an expression meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: A shouted 'Sausage!' leaves the writer sadly upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Say, James going round in the buff?

definitions.text: Say, James going round in the buff?

indicators.note: in means the reversed name goes inside the enthusiast word

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a nut

indicators.note: going round means the name is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Sid James, the Carry On actor, is an example of a James; 'Say' marks him as one

explanation.surface: A man, perhaps called James, wandering about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Sid James was a British comic actor of the Carry On films. 'Going round' turns SID into DIS, which goes 'in' NUT; 'in the buff' also means naked, so the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, which is exactly what being in the buff describes.

clue.text: Given a suitable role, produce manuscript when entering court

parts.note: to type is to produce a manuscript

indicators.note: entering means the word for when goes inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: An actor is cast fittingly, as typing turns up in a courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Typecast means repeatedly assigned the same kind of part, one matched to an actor's image.

clue.text: Pub always admits old women? Not at all

indicators.note: admits means the pub-and-always pair lets other letters in between them

parts.note: an inn is a pub
AY (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A pub that always lets old women in? Certainly not.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (also spelt aye) is an old poetic word for always, as in 'for ay'. 'Admits' puts the old women inside, splitting pub from always.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic negative, meaning by no means or in no respect.

clue.text: Odd leg's twitching — maybe an Alsatian's pulling it

indicators.note: a twitching leg jerks about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the letters of ODD LEGS used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A strange twitching leg, possibly from a German shepherd dragging something along.
explanation.definitionFit: A sled pulled by dogs; an Alsatian is a breed of dog that could be one of the team.

clue.text: Daffy longed, I heard, for another duck

indicators.note: daffy means crazy, so the letters of longed go mad and rearrange; it also echoes Daffy Duck

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

indicators.note: heard says the word I is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the pronoun I, said aloud

explanation.surface: Daffy Duck says he longed for some other duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daffy' looks like the cartoon duck, hence 'another duck', but it is the anagram signal: LONGED becomes GOLDEN. Then 'I heard' gives EYE, which sounds like I.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldeneye is a diving duck, named for its yellow iris; Daffy is the first duck of the surface.

clue.text: Clever technology reversed doctor's feet

indicators.note: reversed says the letters for clever technology are turned back to front

parts.note: AI, artificial intelligence, is clever technology
MB is a medical degree (Bachelor of Medicine), so a doctor; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Smart technology went backwards, as did the doctor's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' are not body parts here but metrical feet in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable, so iambs are poetic feet.

clue.text: Classical character as written showing 16's talent

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a classical character
sic is the Latin tag meaning thus, as written, used to flag a quotation copied exactly

explanation.surface: A character from the classics, shown exactly as written, reveals the talent of someone in clue 16.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is John Coltrane, the jazz saxophonist, whose gift was for this.
explanation.definitionFit: John Coltrane was a jazz saxophonist, so his gift lay in playing and composing tunes.

clue.text: Inky book fills fuel shortage

indicators.note: fills means the book letter goes into the fuel-and-shortage pair

parts.note: coal is a fuel
lack means shortage

explanation.surface: A book makes up for a lack of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fills' puts the book's letter into the middle of the two-word fuel shortage.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal-black means intensely dark, the colour of ink.

clue.text: Agree one should include 'sea', as said to editor

indicators.note: should include means the word for one must take other letters inside it

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards or on a die

indicators.note: as said means the word sea is spoken, giving the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word sea, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that the word 'sea' should go in, as suggested to the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As said' means sea is heard, giving the letter that sounds like it; 'should include' puts that and the editor inside the card word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent or give in to it.

clue.text: Surprisingly lean actor, not a great improviser

indicators.note: surprisingly means unexpectedly, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
not means one letter of the fodder is left out

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
the letter left out

explanation.surface: An actor who is surprisingly thin, not a great improviser.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Robbie Coltrane, the large Scottish actor; the definition is John Coltrane, the jazz saxophonist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Coltrane was a jazz saxophonist, celebrated for long, inventive solos.

clue.text: Novel flares, a result of combustion in the open air

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: the fodder taken as written
CO, carbon monoxide, is produced by burning

explanation.surface: New flares, plus the fumes from burning, outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is Italian for outdoors, used of eating or events held outside.

clue.text: Fat comic character listening to deceitful servants

indicators.note: listening to means the next words are heard, not read

parts.note: false means deceitful; staff are servants

explanation.surface: A fat comedic figure hears about treacherous servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat, boastful knight in Henry IV and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Colourful picture of English history learner absorbs

indicators.note: absorbs means the history-and-learner pair takes another letter into itself

parts.note: the past is history
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A colourful image of English history that a student takes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbs' puts E between PAST and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a drawing made with coloured chalk crayons, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: Heading west in small unexplored ravine

indicators.note: Heading west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the words small unexplored

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Travelling west into a small, uncharted gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no indicator for the hidden word; 'in' is that signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nulla (or nullah) is an Indian and Australian word for a dry watercourse or gully.

clue.text: Actor in the wings with ABC containing current language

indicators.note: in the wings means only the outside letters of actor, as a stage's wings are at its sides

parts.note: taken for its first and last letters

indicators.note: containing means the letters ABC hold the current letter

parts.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An actor waiting offstage beside the ABC network that carries a current tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the Semitic tongue spoken across the Middle East and North Africa.

clue.text: Actor great as 18 every year, his career peaks?

parts.note: Antony Sher, the British actor, was acclaimed as Falstaff
PA is per annum, every year

explanation.surface: An actor praised as Falstaff, year after year: are his career highs at their summit?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career peaks' sounds like professional highs; read literally, it is a mountain guide's working life on summits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan mountaineers and guides whose work takes them up high summits.

clue.text: Without a bit of towel, bather's back drying out

indicators.note: without means a letter is taken away
back means the word bather is turned backwards

parts.note: the word bather, the 's being a link (bather is)

indicators.note: a bit of means only the first letter of towel

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bather's back is drying, though without a towel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns BATHER into REHTAB; 'Without a bit of towel' removes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is treatment for addiction, and 'drying out' is the idiom for getting off alcohol.

clue.text: Animals paired regularly in bible, work of Noah and sons

indicators.note: in means the alternate letters go inside the bible abbreviation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of paired is taken

parts.note: the even letters of paired
Noah built the ark
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Animals in pairs, in the Bible, in Noah's and his sons' handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes A, R, D from paired; these go 'in' AV, the Authorised Version of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Aardvarks are burrowing African mammals, a kind of creature.

clue.text: No money for more bananas, one calculates

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: bananas means mad, so more bananas is madder

explanation.surface: No cash to buy any more bananas, someone works out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like fruit but is slang for crazy, so 'more bananas' is MADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An adder is a machine or person that adds up figures.

clue.text: Rev motor giving six a lift

indicators.note: giving a lift means, in this down clue, the six goes above the motor
a lift is a ride, here the six riding on top of the motor

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
car is a motor

explanation.surface: Revving a car engine to offer six people a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a verb for engines but is the clergy title.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev is the abbreviation of Reverend, the title of a vicar or other cleric.

clue.text: Local employee saving master's papers

parts.note: saving means except, as does bar
MA is a Master of Arts degree
ID, identity documents, are papers

explanation.surface: A local worker hangs on to her boss's documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for the neighbourhood pub, so a local employee works behind its bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmaid serves drinks in a pub, which Britons call their local.

clue.text: A coin is liquid capital

indicators.note: liquid means flowing, so the letters run into a new order

parts.note: the fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A coin counts as liquid assets in finance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquid capital' reads as cash, but 'liquid' is the anagram signal and 'capital' is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Joke I can't remember's a really good one

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a joke
er is the hesitating sound of someone who can't remember

explanation.surface: Someone insists that the joke they have forgotten was a brilliant one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' is informal British for an excellent thing or person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a cracker is something outstanding, a corker or belter.

clue.text: Cancel railway from France after heading for Calais

indicators.note: after means the railway, from and France pieces come behind the Calais letter
heading for means just the first letter of Calais

parts.note: the French port, taken for its first letter
of means from, as in a man of Kent
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: Calling off a train journey from France on its way to Calais.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry off is an idiom for withdrawing from an arrangement or backing out.
